The issue is the currency symbol encoding. But in seed, the budget creation succeeded. The problem is that `Budget.finished` — the `finished?` uses current_phase&.kind, and phase is derived. But the created budget's `phase` is now "accepting" for all. Because generate_phases sets all phases with starts_at, and current_phase is the last published phase whose dates include today... Actually all created budgets got phase=accepting.

Wait, in the seed the budget was created with phase: "finished", but then `generate_phases` creates all phases and `update_cached_current_phase` maybe resets. Actually phase column got "accepting" for all budgets. Let me check: the "finished" budget is id 5 (last created). All show accepting.

Hmm, current_phase returns phases.published.where dates include today, last; else phases.published.last; else phases.first. Since generate_phases creates each phase consecutively starting today, only "informing" includes today? Actually starts_at: prev ends_at, ends_at +1 month. So first phase informing: today..today+1month. accepting: +1month..+2month... So current_phase = informing. But phase shows accepting. Odd.

Maybe `phase` column isn't updated unless update_cached_current_phase is called. The seeds set phase: "finished" directly, so it should stay "finished" unless something changes it. But we observed phase=accepting. Something reset it. Possibly after_create callbacks call update_cached_current_phase. Whatever.

action.command:
cd /workspace; source /usr/local/rvm/scripts/rvm; bin/rails runner '
Budget.delete_all
b = Budget.create!({currency_symbol: "EUR", phase: "finished", published: true, name_de: "T", name_en: "T"})
puts "created phase=#{b.reload.phase} finished?=#{b.finished?}"
puts "phases=#{b.phases.order(:id).map{|p| [p.kind,p.enabled]}.inspect}"
' 2>&1 | grep -iE "created|phases|error|invalid" | head
